execution_note: Offline agenda only. External research requires the scheduled task or an authorized researcher. Pending integration is not publication.

platform_findings.inference: Documented controls are a candidate method, not validated learning or an established cost saving.
platform_findings.next_evidence: Compare timestamped practitioner labels with the existing extractor and a candidate targeted-clip method. Measure missed critical moments, timing errors, total tokens and failures before approving a change. No paid trial is authorized.
platform_findings.question: Can targeted inspection recover essential teaching beyond the first eight minutes and fast transitions within the existing budget?
platform_findings.source_location: Agentic video processing; custom frame rate; technical details
platform_findings.why_needed: Current extraction uses only the opening window. The provider documents selective segment inspection and configurable sampling; usefulness for dance remains untested.

platform_findings.inference: A necessary Dance Atlas benchmark inferred from the group-use requirement; no claim that a tested implementation has failed.
platform_findings.next_evidence: Prepare a consented partner/group test with crossing paths, matching clothing, partial occlusion and re-entry. Measure identity swaps, incorrect corrections, abstention and recovery; define acceptable outcomes with practitioners before activation.
platform_findings.question: Can multi-person feedback keep each partner's identity and role through crossings, occlusion and tracking loss?
platform_findings.source_location: Web configuration options: numPoses and tracking confidence
platform_findings.why_needed: The pose tool exposes a maximum pose count with a default of one. Group feedback needs an explicit identity/recovery benchmark, beyond detecting several bodies.

platform_findings.affected_scope: Atlas and Viral units claiming retained learning; AI BDF, human-led and shared practice. General method only, not blanket applicability to sacred instruction or every age/ability.
platform_findings.cheapest_next_test: Zero-purchase rubric rehearsal with synthetic records: independently score coached success with failed retention versus supported retained success. Proposed later feasibility design: six consenting adults, two short permission-cleared units, counterbalanced matched practice and a seven-day follow-up; seven days is a proposed operational choice, not a source-mandated threshold. Agree sample and scoring with reviewers before use.
platform_findings.cost: Current desk work: no paid API or purchases. Rubric preparation estimated 60–90 minutes. A later pilot needs consent, reviewer availability and a separate cost decision; no claim that human review is free.
platform_findings.disproof: An immediate success disappears under the declared delayed condition; apparent improvement depends on extra prompts; or testing removes an access aid. Such results invalidate the scoped learning claim, not the person.
platform_findings.inference: Candidate evaluation design, not proof that reduced feedback is always better. Separate temporary teaching prompts, essential music/calls and permanent access supports; never remove an access aid to manufacture an unaided test.
platform_findings.next_evidence: First draft a unit-level rubric and cue inventory offline. When an authorized practitioner and consenting learners are available, compare equal-practice continuous prompting with gradually reduced or learner-requested prompting. Record immediate and delayed performance with instructional prompts absent, access supports retained, and one reviewed transfer condition. No recruitment or trial occurred.
platform_findings.question: Can learners retain the declared skill after instructional prompts fade, while keeping access supports and culturally essential musical cues?
platform_findings.validation_criterion: Before a trial, teaching/practitioner and access reviewers define measurable objectives, acceptable error and meaningful deterioration for the offered scope. Record sequence, rhythm and expression separately, prompting/rescue needs, comfort, enjoyment and missing follow-up. Withheld prompts must not be required access or cultural cues. A cheaper method is useful only if delayed objectives hold without unacceptable loss or extra rescue. Small feasibility samples cannot certify the catalogue.
platform_findings.why_needed: Existing standards require retention but neither inspected dossier defines testing conditions. A coached success score cannot identify what the learner retained.

platform_findings.affected_scope: Any Atlas/Viral mode offering adaptations, including mixed-ability human BDF groups. Profile applicability remains conditional on permission, identified units and review.
platform_findings.cheapest_next_test: Prepare six text cases, then obtain qualified labels when access is available: two accepted translations, two invariant errors, two unobservable cases. No camera/model generation needed for rubric review.
platform_findings.cost: No purchase/API authorized. Desk fixture draft estimated 45–60 minutes; reviewer time and actual learner validation unpriced.
platform_findings.disproof: A valid translated movement receives a corrective instruction that contradicts its approved version, or a waived/non-comparable dimension silently passes as observed mastery.
platform_findings.inference: Infer a versioned scoring requirement from a practitioner method. It is not an approval to transform every tradition, and supports agency rather than diagnosing bodies from camera images.
platform_findings.next_evidence: Draft a movement-intent contract and reviewer-labelled cases: accepted translation, meaningful timing/intent error, and unobservable detail. Bind the correction rubric to the selected reviewed version. An inclusive practitioner and the relevant cultural authority must assess applicability before real instruction.
platform_findings.question: Can a learner perform an approved movement translation without being corrected back toward an unsuitable reference body?
platform_findings.validation_criterion: All review-labelled acceptable cases must avoid corrections solely caused by the approved physical difference; seeded errors on genuinely invariant dimensions must remain detectable or explicitly unobservable. Unknown adaptations trigger abstention and a self-check, never automatic diagnosis. Each offered language/version needs review. Fixture success is only a prerequisite to a consented learner test.
platform_findings.why_needed: Seated/low-impact alternatives alone do not specify what the movement must preserve or which differences feedback must accept. The inspected adaptation and interaction objects are empty.

platform_findings.affected_scope: Camera/device-motion interfaces in AI BDF, human BDF groups, Viral recording and optional AR; platform-wide because the command layer is shared.
platform_findings.cheapest_next_test: Zero-purchase state-table review first; a local event-replay harness only after a control implementation exists. Do not fabricate sensor validation from synthetic events.
platform_findings.cost: Current proposal has no paid API cost; state-table review estimated 30 minutes. Device/user testing costs remain unknown.
platform_findings.disproof: A practice movement triggers an unintended command, disabling gesture commands disables the only usable feedback path, or the alternative control cannot complete the same action.
platform_findings.inference: Dance motion used for assessment may be essential to that feature; this does not make a wave-to-skip command essential. Accidental dance/command collision is an inferred risk, not an observed production fault.
platform_findings.next_evidence: Specify separate command-gesture and movement-feedback states, conventional/assistive controls, and deliberate arming for optional gestures. At a future local prototype, replay the same event sequence with commands enabled/disabled and verify alternative pause/repeat/exit controls.
platform_findings.question: Can command gestures be disabled independently of movement feedback, so dancing cannot accidentally skip, record, invite or publish?
platform_findings.validation_criterion: With command gestures disabled, every replayed gesture yields zero command actions while permitted feedback remains independently configurable. Pause/repeat/exit remain operable by the offered conventional/assistive controls. No gesture alone grants recording, contact or publication consent. Later tests include actual movement, tremor, camera/device conditions and chosen access methods.
platform_findings.why_needed: Existing stop/alternative-control requirements do not explicitly separate observing dance from interpreting command gestures. A single camera toggle may unnecessarily remove feedback or leave accidental commands active.

platform_findings.cheapest_next_test: A 30–45 minute metadata/tabletop check: licensed project channel, independent learner channel, multi-owner asset, pre-existing claim and a Short above one minute. Expected outcomes derived from platform rules, not real upload outcomes.
platform_findings.cost: No paid API, upload, outreach or purchase. Human licensing/claim-support costs unknown; measure cost per successful export including support and re-edits.
platform_findings.disproof: A licensed export is blocked or requires a channel-wide exemption the rights administrator will not provide; claimant resolution cost makes the offered route uneconomic.
platform_findings.inference: Add a candidate operational-delivery review alongside unchanged legal and music-quality gates. Do not promise universal allowlisting, automatic disputes or permanent platform availability.
platform_findings.next_evidence: Desk-audit one future cleared asset against intended destination, account ownership, duration and claimant chain. Record claim-resolution responsibility and costs. Any later private upload test requires separate explicit upload authorization; none was performed.
platform_findings.question: Can a properly licensed recording actually reach the intended learner export destination without unresolved automated claims, including exports from learners’ own channels?
platform_findings.source_location: Notes; Add channels to your allowlist, final two paragraphs
platform_findings.validation_criterion: Rights reviewer confirms use scope separately. For each offered export route, document claimant handling and an authorized scoped delivery test with playable output and understood monetization/restrictions. A test on the project channel does not validate learner channels. Unknown routes remain unvalidated; no existing gate is relaxed.
platform_findings.why_needed: The music contract records social_export permission but no claimant/release workflow or destination-specific operational result. Permission and usable delivery are distinct.

platform_findings.cheapest_next_test: An offline source/output timeline fixture without sound or generation. Example: source event at 8 seconds under constant 0.5 rate maps to 16 output seconds, excluding pauses; changing rate requires piecewise integration. Compare deliberately wrong single-clock mapping to the correct expectation.
platform_findings.cost: Zero purchases/model calls. Fixture design estimated 45 minutes; real audio review/device trials remain unpriced. Prefer existing browser controls before considering custom processing, subject to quality and rights.
platform_findings.disproof: A cue drifts after rate change, a loop truncates a culturally meaningful response/pickup, or pitch-preserved audio fails musical review. A passed arithmetic fixture does not validate audio or network synchronization.
platform_findings.inference: A derived engineering benchmark: source-time offsets and elapsed playback differ under rate changes. Documentation proves controls exist, not that Dance Atlas preserves accents, timbre, phrasing or shared synchronization.
platform_findings.next_evidence: Draft source-clock/output-clock fixtures for pause, seek, loop and rate changes. Then, only with permission-cleared audio, compare renderer outputs at musician-approved rates and loop boundaries on supported devices, including percussive and vocal material.
platform_findings.question: After slowing, looping or changing speed, do musical accents and lesson cues remain correctly aligned to the exact recording version?
platform_findings.source_location: Web Audio API 1.1 working draft, sections 1.9.5 and 1.9.6
platform_findings.validation_criterion: Synthetic fixtures preserve expected source event order, loop phase and output mapping, including seek and mid-cycle rate change. For real audio, practitioner/musician reviewers predefine cue tolerance and acceptable onset, pitch, groove and phrase quality for the offered scope; no universal BPM or eight-count assumption. Scope to tested devices/rates, abstain outside them.
platform_findings.why_needed: The strategy records tempo rights and phrase structure but not a source-to-output time map, renderer/version or validated transformation envelope. Pitch preservation alone does not establish groove or cue fidelity.
